sections.h2: Where is Sherwood, Arkansas, and what kind of housing market is it?
sections.html:
Sherwood is a city in Pulaski County, part of the Little Rock-North Little Rock-Conway metro area. Its ZIP code is 72120, and Arkansas Highway 107 runs through it.

The town was incorporated on April 22, 1948. It became a second-class city on September 16, 1957 and a first-class city on April 30, 1971. The former Gravel Ridge area was annexed on April 28, 2008, and the city's first and second wards were created from that annexed area. The Census Bureau counted 32,731 residents in 2020 and estimates 33,620 for July 1, 2025, up from 21,511 in 2000.

For a seller, the useful point is that Sherwood is mostly an owner-occupied suburb. The table below uses Census Bureau QuickFacts figures for 2020 to 2024.

A 70.8 percent ownership rate means most of the houses you see on a Sherwood street are lived in by their owners. Rental houses and inherited houses are the minority, and they are where condition problems tend to pile up.

sections.h2: What did the March 2023 tornado do to Sherwood homes?
sections.html:
The National Weather Service rated the March 31, 2023 tornado EF3, with estimated peak winds of 165 mph, and its track went straight through Sherwood. The storm stayed on the ground for 34.4 miles, from northwest of Alexander in Pulaski County to southeast of Austin in Lonoke County, and reached a maximum width of 600 yards.

The survey says it crossed John F. Kennedy Boulevard near Club Road, moved northeast through Sherwood generally along Lee Avenue, and damaged many homes. It then continued toward Kiehl Avenue and damaged more homes and some businesses near Northgate Drive and Woodridge Lane. The report is preliminary and does not break injuries down by city, so we leave out any Sherwood-only casualty figure.

Why does this matter when you sell? Three practical things come up on houses along that track:

  • Roof and decking repairs that were done quickly after the storm may not have permits or final inspections on file.
  • Insurance claim paperwork, contractor invoices and warranties are worth gathering, because a buyer or lender will ask for them.
  • Houses with unfinished repairs can be hard to finance through a conventional loan, which is one reason owners look at an as-is sale.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Sherwood, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Sherwood has a humid subtropical climate, with hot summers, mild winters and about 50 inches of rain a year. The 1981 to 2010 normals show a July average high of 92 degrees and a January average low of 33 degrees. Records run from 110 degrees in July 1986 to minus 6 degrees in January 1985.

Heat and moisture are the main wear factors. Air conditioning systems work hard through long summers, and roofs take both sun and storm damage. Buyers who walk through a Sherwood house tend to look at the age of the roof, the HVAC unit and any signs of water intrusion first. If those three items are old, a cash sale to an investor who prices the repairs in is often simpler than spending your own money before listing.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads serve Sherwood?
sections.html:
Public schools in Sherwood belong to the Pulaski County Special School District, whose boundary takes in the entire city including the old Gravel Ridge area. The public high school is Sylvan Hills High School, and the district also runs Sylvan Hills Middle School and four Sherwood elementary schools: Clinton Speech Communications and Technology Magnet, Oakbrooke, Sherwood and Sylvan Hills. LISA Academy North is a public charter school that opened in 2008.

The Sylvan Hills High School building dates to 2020, and the middle school moved to a 44-acre campus across Highway 107 in fall 2011. Neither fact sets a price, but a listing that names the school zone is easier for a buyer to place.

Cars are the main way to get around. The commute figure above, 24.1 minutes, reflects the fact that many residents work in Little Rock or North Little Rock. The city also lists bike and walking paths and 14 parks, among them Sherwood's Henson Park, Pickthorne Park, Austin Lake Park and Thornhill Park.

Health care and call-center work are the employers most often named for Sherwood, along with the city and school district. CHI St. Vincent North Hospital is a 69-bed nonprofit hospital with a Level IV trauma center, and a 60-bed rehabilitation hospital sits alongside it. Customer contact centers for FTD.com and Cardinal Health have also been listed for the city. Employer lists change, so confirm current headcounts with the city or the chamber before relying on them.

The city government uses a mayor-council form. Its mayor serves four-year terms, and the council has eight aldermen. The Sherwood police department dates to 1964 and the fire department to 1950.

sections.h2: What permits and city offices matter when selling a Sherwood house?
sections.html:
Building permits in Sherwood go through the city's Permits and Planning staff, who can be reached at 501-835-4753 on weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The directory lists a Chief Building Official, a building inspector, a city planner and permit clerks. The city website also has a permits portal and downloadable forms for residential building, electrical and plumbing permits.

If you have done work without a permit, such as a deck, an addition or a roof replacement after the tornado, ask the office what a late permit would take before the house goes under contract. A buyer's inspector will often notice the gap.

Common seller tasks in Sherwood look like this:

  • Pull the permit history for any structural, electrical or plumbing work.
  • Confirm that city utilities are active, since the city lists utility sign-up and a trash schedule on its site.
  • Check the parcel record at the Pulaski County assessor for the correct owner and mailing address.
  • Gather the deed, and for an inherited house, the court papers that give you authority to sign.

sections.h2: How does property tax work on a Sherwood house?
sections.html:
Sherwood houses are taxed by Pulaski County, the school district and the city, and the bill is due October 15 each year in Arkansas. The Arkansas Assessment Coordination Division says counties reappraise every three, four or five years. Owners who disagree with a value should start with the county assessor, because errors in property details can often be fixed without a formal appeal. A hearing before the county Board of Equalization must be requested by the third Monday in August.

A Pulaski County reappraisal covered by local news raised many values, with owners facing a cap of up to 5 percent a year on owner-occupied homes and up to 10 percent on rentals. Owners 65 or older and disabled owners can ask the assessor to freeze their assessed value. If you are selling mid-year, ask the title company how the current year's tax will be split at closing.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a house in Arkansas?
sections.html:
Arkansas charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual consideration on deeds and similar instruments. On a $100,000 sale that works out to $330, according to the Department of Finance and Administration. The agency page does not say which party pays, so settle that in the contract and confirm it with the closing agent.

That fee is small next to a listing commission or repair costs, but it is a reminder that every route to closing has line items. A written cash offer should show them all so you can compare what you actually net.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Sherwood?
sections.html:
A cash sale tends to fit when the house needs repairs a lender would not accept, when the owner wants a firm closing date, or when the property came through probate. A conventional listing can still bring a higher price on a house in good shape, and it is worth asking an agent for an opinion before you decide.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as-is across Arkansas. We cannot promise a number before we have seen the details, so the offer is written after you tell us about the house and we run the figures. You can compare it with a listing estimate and choose.

faqs.q: How many people live in Sherwood, Arkansas?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 33,620 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 32,731 and the 2000 census counted 21,511.
Sherwood is in Pulaski County. Property tax is billed through the county, so the Pulaski County assessor and collector handle your parcel, while the city handles permits.
Yes. The National Weather Service survey says the EF3 tornado of March 31, 2023 moved northeast through Sherwood generally along Lee Avenue and damaged many homes, then continued toward Kiehl Avenue.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Arkansas?
faqs.a: October 15 each year. Late real estate payments carry penalties and interest, so confirm the current amount with the county collector.

faqs.q: What does the Arkansas transfer tax cost?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of the sale price on a deed. On $100,000 that is $330. Agree in the contract who pays it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sherwood house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers who pay cash often purchase houses as-is, so repairs like roofing, HVAC and storm damage do not have to be finished before closing.
